subject: VPC patch rotation + abort criteria — upgrade runbook for Acme Health
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:00:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: VPC patch rotation and abort criteria — Acme Health (please review)

Team / Sanjay,

Attached is a first-pass runbook for the upcoming Private deployment patch window for Acme Health (attached: redwood_vpc_upgrade_runbook_v1.pdf). High level: we need a staggered rotation across three availability groups, preflight checks at boot, KV cache warmup, and an explicit abort ladder (fast abort vs degrade-to-fallback).

Specific asks:
- Karthik: sanity-check the canary cadence and health-check thresholds (I sketched 10% fleet -> 30% -> full).
- Vivek: confirm network-level maintenance ordering (switching NATs, BGP prep) and whether we should block external control-plane changes during the first two waves.
- Hannah: ops comm template and post-mortem header.
- Sanjay / Acme: confirm your preferred 2–4 hour maintenance window options and any disallowed blackout periods for your monitoring overlays.

Key constraints I put in the doc:
- Maintain RTO goal of 5m for control-plane API and 99.9% availability for inference traffic during window (target-throughput degrade allowed to 75%).
- Abort triggers (draft): component reboot errors > 3 nodes in group OR KV cache miss-rate spike > +2.5 percentage points sustained > 3 minutes OR end-to-end p95 latency > baseline + 1200ms for two consecutive windows.

I left an empty appendix for any vendor certs/tests Acme needs to collect. If we agree on the triggers we can lock the schedule and book a tabletop rehearsal.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft: VPC patch rotation and abort criteria — Acme Health (please review)

Laura — good baseline. A few nit/ops notes below; I embedded them into the runbook but pasting the highlights here so they aren’t missed:

- Canary cadence: prefer three waves [5%, 25%, 100%] rather than 10/30/60. Smaller first wave reduces blast radius and gives faster signal for KV warmup metrics.
- Health checks: recommend these concrete, machine-measurable checks:
  * node_agent_online == true for >= 90% of nodes in wave within 4m
  * deploy_agent_restart_count == 0 for 3m rolling window OR else fast-abort
  * kv_cache_hit_rate (per-shard) not dropping more than 2.5 percentage points relative to preflight baseline (calculated over 5m)
- Abort ladder (clarified):
  * Fast abort (immediate rollback): any semantic failure in the control plane (API auth failures, datastore corruption signatures) OR node reboot loop >= 3 nodes in 2m.
  * Managed degrade (pause + partial rollback): sustained p95 increase > baseline + 900ms AND error-rate increase > 0.6% for 5m -> pause and roll back last wave only.
  * Escalate to customer (manual hold): configuration drift detected on >1 VLAN or BGP peers flapping during the wave.
- Network ordering: we should perform non-disruptive kernel/driver patches only after we complete NAT/BGP validation. If a NIC firmware update is required, it must be scheduled as a separate window (we mark as "firmware-blocking" in the spreadsheet).

I also added a short section on the 'fail-open' vs 'fail-close' behavior for KV cache population for model shards. We should prefer fail-open for inference traffic with traffic-shaping to avoid full outage.

I can join a call Thurs 11:00 PST to walk through.

-Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Laura / team,

Thanks for the runbook. A few notes from Acme Ops: we can support a 03:00–06:00 PST window on Saturdays (preferred) or Sundays; weekdays are not possible due to live reporting. Please note the following constraints we need you to capture in the final doc:

- Network change advisory: any BGP peer flaps must be communicated at T-24hrs and T-1hr at minimum to our NOC; if BGP peer downtime exceeds 90s during a wave we require an automatic rollback.
- Control plane SLAs: Acme requires a signed maintenance exception in our contract if control-plane RTO > 10m during the window. We are OK with brief, sub-10m degradations but want the exception documented.
- Monitoring hooks: we will provide a temporary read-only Prometheus endpoint for the runbook rehearsal. Please ensure the playbook includes the endpoint and the exact metric names (we saw the kv_cache_hit_rate name in the doc — that's correct).

I attached the network matrix with our VLAN/peer details. Happy to do a dry run next week if you want.

-sanjay

- Sanjay: once you confirm the Saturday 03:00–06:00 PST window we’ll reserve the slot and schedule a tabletop rehearsal (30–45m) using your temporary Prom endpoint.
